topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the key learning objectives regarding cancer therapies and their modes of action.

topics.label: Conventional Interventions, Cytotoxic Chemotherapy, and Multidrug Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the principles, toxicities, and drug resistance mechanisms associated with conventional cancer treatments such as surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic agents.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Vulnerabilities: Hormone Pathways, Checkpoint Defects, and Synthetic Lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic approaches that target specific cancer vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell-cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Targeting Oncogenic Kinases, Resistance Mechanisms, and Drug Addiction
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the design of small-molecule inhibitors targeting oncogenic driver kinases and examine the molecular mechanisms driving drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Targeted Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms, design, and therapeutic applications of monoclonal antibodies and toxin-linked antibody conjugates.

topics.label: Tumour Immunology, Checkpoint Blockade, and Engineered Cell Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine natural immune surveillance and various immunotherapeutic strategies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Systemic Challenges, Historical Trends, and Future Paradigms in Cancer Care
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate broad clinical challenges, epidemiological progress, emerging paradigms, and ethical dilemmas in modern oncology.
